methodological_rigor.justification: This is a large derivation-plus-external-validation prognostic study across multiple international cohorts, which is an appropriate design for staging-system development. The main weakness is that the longitudinal strain threshold was selected in the derivation set with support from prior reports and ROC analysis, so some optimism and center-level heterogeneity remain possible. The statistical work is otherwise strong, with multivariable modeling, collinearity checks, and calibration/discrimination analyses all reported.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Oxford LoE 2b fits an individual cohort/prognostic validation study. The clinical relevance is high because the staging system directly refines prognosis, risk stratification, and trial selection in systemic AL amyloidosis, especially for the new IIIC ultra-poor-risk group. It is not practice-changing by itself, but it has immediate translational value for counseling and trial design.

reporting_quality.justification: TRIPOD is the best fit because the manuscript develops and externally validates a prognostic staging model, and the core model-performance elements are present: calibration, discrimination, and external validation across multiple cohorts. The manuscript is detailed, but it does not describe public code or data release, so reproducibility is moderate. Minor omissions relate mainly to the absence of a transparent sharing statement in the blinded text.

novelty_literature.justification: The main novelty is the addition of longitudinal strain to established cardiac biomarker staging, creating a new IIIC ultra-poor-risk category in the modern treatment era. That is a meaningful extension of prior Mayo and European staging work and goes beyond a simple reanalysis of old thresholds. It is still an incremental prognostic advance rather than a new biological mechanism or therapy.

writing_presentation.justification: The paper is well structured and the abstract efficiently summarizes the derivation, validation, and performance metrics. The results are numerically detailed and the figure captions make the staging and calibration plots interpretable. Some prose is dense and repeats prior staging history, but the presentation is strong.

key_strengths: Large international derivation and validation cohorts.
Useful new staging category that sharpens risk discrimination in modern AL amyloidosis.
Calibration and discrimination are reported clearly and support the model.
key_concerns: Threshold selection in the derivation set still invites optimism bias.
Center-level heterogeneity and referral bias are hard to exclude.
No public data or code release is described.
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a strong prognostic validation paper with clear clinical utility and a well-supported new staging category. Tier 2 is plausible, and minor revisions are enough at that level.
